letterforms.title: Letterforms and words
letterforms.description: Letter spacing, font metrics, ligatures, and word breaks.

noResults: No matching terms. Try another word.
headline: Ideas become things.
readingText: Good typography gives each idea room to breathe. The space between lines and the length of each line shape the rhythm of reading. Change one setting and notice how the same words feel different.
longTitle: A small guide to making thoughtful things
metricsNote: Same font size. The guides follow the measured x or H glyph in your browser.
kerningNote: Only AI and vC move; the other gaps stay the same.
opticalNote: The upper row is the reference. One toggle applies the whole-word optical preset below; multiple gaps change together, with exaggerated differences.
smoothingNote: The effect depends on your browser and display. Some systems show no visible change.

kerning.title: Kerning
kerning.description: Adjusting the spacing of a chosen character pair. It corrects uneven gaps without changing every gap, as tracking does.

tracking.title: Tracking
tracking.description: Uniform letter spacing across a word or passage. Uppercase labels often need more space to remain readable.

leading.title: Leading
leading.description: The vertical distance between lines. Tight spacing crowds letters; excessive spacing breaks a paragraph’s visual flow.

optical-kerning.title: Optical kerning
optical-kerning.description: Spacing guided by letter shapes and visual balance, instead of relying only on a font’s kerning metrics.

tabular-nums.title: Tabular numerals
tabular-nums.description: A font feature that gives digits equal widths, keeping prices, statistics and changing numeric columns aligned.

type-scale.title: Type scale
type-scale.description: A defined set of font sizes, often linked by a ratio, that keeps headings and body text in a consistent hierarchy.

weight.title: Font weight
weight.description: The thickness of letter strokes, used for emphasis and interface hierarchy. Change the title weight and compare it with regular body text.

x-height.title: X-height
x-height.description: The height of a lowercase letter like x, relative to the cap height. A high x-height makes a font feel larger at the same point size, which is why two fonts at 16px can look very different in size.

cap-height.title: Cap height
cap-height.description: The height of capitals above the baseline. Compare it with x-height when pairing typefaces or choosing fallback fonts.

ligature.title: Ligature
ligature.description: A glyph combining characters such as fi or fl to prevent collisions. Decorative ligatures are better suited to display text.

font-smoothing.title: Font smoothing
font-smoothing.description: How text edges are rendered. On macOS, antialiased rendering may appear thinner; the result depends on the browser and display.

text-overflow.title: Text overflow
text-overflow.description: Text exceeding its container. An ellipsis (…) can signal clipped text; wrapping instead preserves content when additional lines are possible.

hyphenation.title: Hyphenation
hyphenation.description: Breaking words between lines with hyphens. It helps narrow or justified text; automatic break points depend on the language and browser.

clamp.title: Clamp
clamp.description: Fluid sizing bounded by minimum, preferred and maximum values. It lets text scale with space without separate rules at every breakpoint.

widow.title: Widow
widow.description: A single word left alone on the last line of a paragraph. text-wrap: balance can fix it automatically.

orphan.title: Orphan
orphan.description: A paragraph’s first line isolated at a page or column’s bottom. Keep it with following lines to preserve reading continuity.

font-stack.title: Font stack
font-stack.description: An ordered list of preferred and fallback fonts. Similar proportions reduce reflow when the browser swaps fonts.

line-length.title: Line length
line-length.description: The width of a text column. Around 65 characters is a starting point for Latin text; adjust for language and typeface.

variable-font.title: Variable font
variable-font.description: One font file with adjustable axes such as weight and width. It can replace several static font files and support smooth variations.

superscript.title: Superscript
superscript.description: Raised characters for exponents or footnotes. Adjust size and vertical position carefully so the surrounding line spacing stays stable.

subscript.title: Subscript
subscript.description: Lowered characters for chemical formulas or notation. Size and vertical position should preserve the surrounding line’s rhythm.

srgb.title: sRGB
srgb.description: The standard color space most screens have used for decades. All hex values live here. Its gamut is limited: there are colors a modern display can show that sRGB cannot describe.

p3.title: P3
p3.description: A wider color space supported by most modern screens. Allows more vivid colors, particularly greens and reds, that sRGB cannot reach.

oklch.title: OKLCH
oklch.description: A color space that matches how humans perceive brightness. Unlike HSL, two colors at the same lightness value actually look the same brightness. Useful for generating palettes and accessible color mixes.

alpha.title: Alpha
alpha.description: The transparency component of a color, from fully opaque to fully invisible. An alpha border recedes into the surface beneath it. A solid hex sits on top. The difference is subtle but consistently felt.

semantic-token.title: Semantic token
semantic-token.description: A color variable named for its purpose rather than its value. --color-border-subtle instead of #e0e0e0. When the value changes, everything using the token updates.

contrast-ratio.title: Contrast ratio
contrast-ratio.description: The luminance difference between a foreground and background color. WCAG requires 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and UI components.

tinted-neutral.title: Tinted neutral
tinted-neutral.description: A grey with a slight hue bias. Pure #808080 looks like a placeholder. A tinted neutral feels chosen.

saturation.title: Saturation
saturation.description: How vivid or muted a color is. Brand colors at full saturation in dark mode can vibrate off the screen. Pulling back 20-30% settles them.

chroma.title: Chroma
chroma.description: The OKLCH equivalent of saturation, but perceptually accurate. Reducing chroma for a light tint keeps the color alive. Reducing opacity does the same but turns it grey and lifeless.

gradient.title: Gradient
gradient.description: A transition between two or more colors. In HSL or sRGB, the midpoint often goes grey. Building gradients in OKLCH keeps the colors vivid throughout.

opacity-vs-visibility.title: Opacity vs visibility
opacity-vs-visibility.description: Two ways to hide an element. Opacity zero still occupies space and receives pointer events. Visibility hidden removes interaction but keeps the space. Worth knowing which you need.

dark-mode.title: Dark mode
dark-mode.description: An interface built on dark surfaces. The brightest surface should sit at the top of the layering hierarchy. Light mode tokens rarely translate directly, so every color decision needs rechecking.

blending.title: Blending
blending.description: How a layer interacts with what’s beneath it. Multiply darkens, Screen lightens, Overlay does both depending on the base color. Useful for integrating images with colored surfaces and adding depth to illustrations.

stroke-weight.title: Stroke weight
stroke-weight.description: How thick the lines of an icon are. Thin strokes disappear at small sizes. At large sizes they look frail. Weight needs to scale with size.

optical-centre.title: Optical centre
optical-centre.description: Where something looks centred versus where it mathematically is. A play button centred by coordinates looks left-heavy. Nudge it right and it sits.

filled-vs-outlined.title: Filled vs outlined
filled-vs-outlined.description: Two icon styles for communicating state. Filled often signals active or selected. Outlined signals default. Mixing both without a clear system creates noise.

cap-style.title: Cap style
cap-style.description: Whether stroke ends are square or round. Round caps feel finished in most UI contexts. Square caps can read as unrefined.

pixel-hinting.title: Pixel hinting
pixel-hinting.description: Adjusting icon paths to sit cleanly on a pixel grid at small sizes. A full-detail logo at 16px turns to mush without it.

icon-library.title: Icon library
icon-library.description: A set of icons drawn at the same size, weight, and radius. Mixing two libraries, even similar ones, creates subtle mismatches that compound across a product.

icon-size-system.title: Icon size system
icon-size-system.description: The defined sizes an icon is designed to appear at, typically 12, 16, 20, 24, and 48px. Each size is ideally drawn or adjusted for that specific context rather than scaled from a single master.

meaning-collision.title: Meaning collision
meaning-collision.description: When the same icon is used for two different actions in the same product. A star used for both favouriting and rating. A chevron used for both expanding and navigating. Users learn neither reliably.

contextual-swap.title: Contextual swap
contextual-swap.description: Switching from an outlined icon to a filled one (or vice versa) to signal a state change like active, selected, or toggled. The convention needs to be consistent across the product to work. Mixed usage means users can’t learn the pattern.

breathing-room.title: Breathing room
breathing-room.description: The space between an icon and its label inside a button or list item. Too close and they look like they collided. 6 to 8px is a reasonable starting point. The gap is part of the component design, not an afterthought.

unified-weight.title: Unified weight
unified-weight.description: When icons and surrounding text share the same visual weight. A thin-stroke icon next to bold text looks like it came from a different product. Icons should feel like they belong to the same visual family as the type beside them.

metaphor-accuracy.title: Metaphor accuracy
metaphor-accuracy.description: Whether the icon actually represents what it’s supposed to. A floppy disk for save, a phone handset for call, a house for home. These work until the generation using them has never seen the physical object. Worth auditing as your audience ages.

colorPreview.p3Note: P3 needs a compatible display and browser. Other screens show the sRGB fallback in both circles.
colorPreview.tokenNote: Change --color-border-subtle to update all three borders together.
colorPreview.contrastNote: WCAG AA: 4.5:1 for body text; 3:1 for large text and UI components.
colorPreview.saturationNote: Try 70–80% saturation on the dark surface. Hue and HSL lightness stay fixed.
colorPreview.chromaNote: Left: raise lightness and lower chroma. Right: lower alpha. The gray background stays the same.
colorPreview.gradientNote: The endpoints stay the same. Compare the color in the middle.
colorPreview.alphaNote: Compare an alpha border with solid #808080 on different surfaces.
colorPreview.visibilityNote: Both keep their space. Only opacity: 0 still accepts clicks and keyboard focus.
colorPreview.darkNote: In the dark palette, each raised surface gets lighter.
colorPreview.blendNote: The colors stay fixed. The blend mode changes their overlap.
colorPreview.oklchNote: Every color in a row shares the same L value. Compare the changes in brightness across each row.

iconPreview.strokeNote: The slider sets the 24px weight. Fixed uses that same stroke at every size; scaled adjusts it with icon size.
iconPreview.opticalNote: The circles and centre guides stay fixed. The optical setting moves the play shape slightly right.
iconPreview.capNote: The path and weight stay the same. Compare the stroke ends at native size and enlarged.
iconPreview.pixelNote: Top: native 16px. Below: the same drawing rasterised at 16 × 16, enlarged 6×. Your display can render native edges differently.
iconPreview.libraryNote: Switch to a consistent set: size, stroke weight and corner treatment align.
iconPreview.sizeNote: Compare a scaled 24px master with size-specific drawings. The 12px version omits the door; other sizes adjust paths and strokes.
iconPreview.gapNote: Try 6–8px, then compare with no gap. The icon and label keep their size.
iconPreview.unifiedNote: The lower label stays bold. Increase its icon stroke to balance the pair; the upper row is the regular-weight reference.
iconPreview.filledNote: Choose a destination. Its icon fills; the others stay outlined.
iconPreview.collisionNote: Both actions start with a star. Give favourites a heart and reserve the star for ratings.
iconPreview.swapNote: Toggle each action. Filled consistently means selected; outlined means unselected.
iconPreview.metaphorNote: Name the three actions, then reveal their labels. Familiar symbols depend on what your audience recognises.
